result.label: Source-read

claims.claim: A debt buyer shall not bring suit to collect a consumer debt if the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer's claim has expired.
claims.quote: A debt buyer shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect a consumer debt if the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer’s claim has expired.
claims.note: The prohibition expressly covers bringing suit.

claims.claim: A debt buyer shall not initiate an arbitration to collect a consumer debt if the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer's claim has expired.
claims.quote: A debt buyer shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect a consumer debt if the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer’s claim has expired.
claims.note: The same condition applies to initiating arbitration.

claims.claim: A debt buyer shall not initiate another legal proceeding to collect a consumer debt if the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer's claim has expired.
claims.quote: A debt buyer shall not bring suit or initiate an arbitration or other legal proceeding to collect a consumer debt if the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer’s claim has expired.
claims.note: The prohibition also expressly covers initiating other legal proceedings.

result.summary: Section 1788.56 supports all three prohibitions under the stated condition: the applicable statute of limitations on the debt buyer’s claim has expired.
